examples.en: The agent answers customers' questions kindly.
I replied to the inquiry email within a day.
I will answer the questions calmly in the interview.
I'm busy now, so it's hard to answer.

examples.ko: 고객센터에서 답변해 주는 데 이틀 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took two days for the customer center to reply.

examples.ko: 선생님이 묻는 말에 솔직하게 답변하면 돼요.
examples.en: Just answer honestly whatever the teacher asks.

explain: '대답하다'는 이름을 부르는 소리에도 쓰지만, '답변하다'는 질문, 문의, 인터뷰처럼 정식으로 물어본 것에 답할 때만 써요. 친구가 부르면 '대답해'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '대답하다' can be used even when someone just calls your name, but '답변하다' is only for answering a real question, inquiry, or interview. If a friend calls you, '대답해' is the natural word.

examples.en: This class is run in a question-and-answer format.
I find question-and-answer explanations easy to understand.
This book is in Q&A form, so it is easy to read.
The reporter wrote an interview article in Q&A form.

examples.ko: 면접이 문답식이 아니라 대화처럼 편하게 진행됐어요.
examples.en: The interview was not a strict Q&A but went comfortably like a conversation.
I memorized words by doing a Q&A-style quiz.

explain: 질문과 대답을 주고받는 방식이라는 뜻으로, 주로 '문답식 수업', '문답식 인터뷰'처럼 방식을 말할 때 붙여 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '질문과 대답'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a format of going back and forth with questions and answers, usually attached to nouns as in '문답식 수업' or '문답식 인터뷰'. In casual talk people may simply say '질문과 대답'.

examples.en: He trailed off, mumbling.
Don't answer vaguely; say it clearly.

examples.ko: 아침부터 어물어물 시간을 보내다 보니 벌써 점심이에요.
examples.en: I dawdled around since morning and now it's already lunchtime.
The child mumbled something vague and went into the room.
Don't try to slip out of it with a vague answer.

examples.ko: 할 말을 못 하고 어물어물 서 있기만 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't say what I wanted and just stood there fumbling.

explain: 말을 분명히 못 하고 얼버무리거나, 행동이 굼뜬 모습에 써요. '얼버무리다', '넘어가다', '대답하다'와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It describes mumbling without saying things clearly, or acting slowly. It often appears with verbs like '얼버무리다', '넘어가다' and '대답하다'.

en: take action; take steps; deal with

examples.en: If a problem comes up, please deal with it right away.
They say the company has already taken action.
I discussed with the team how to handle it.
If we do not act quickly, there will be big trouble.
It took less than a day to deal with it.
I will send you by email what we did about it.

explain: '조치'는 문제가 생겼을 때 해결하려고 하는 행동이에요. '조치하다'도 쓰지만 '필요한 조치를 취하다'처럼 '조치를 취하다'가 더 자주 들려요. 회사 공지나 고객센터 답변에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: '조치' is an action taken to solve a problem. '조치하다' is used, but '조치를 취하다', as in '필요한 조치를 취하다', is heard more often. You often see it in company notices and customer-service replies.

en: ask a question; make an inquiry

examples.ko: 발표가 끝나면 청중이 연사에게 질의할 수 있어요.
examples.en: After the presentation, the audience can ask the speaker questions.
The lawmaker questioned the minister about the policy.
Please send any questions you have by email.

examples.ko: 회의 마지막에 담당자에게 질의하는 시간이 있어요.
examples.en: There is time at the end of the meeting to ask the person in charge questions.

examples.ko: 교수님께 질의하기 전에 질문을 미리 정리해 두세요.
examples.en: Organize your questions in advance before you put them to the professor.

examples.ko: 시청에 전화해서 신청 방법을 질의하려고 해요.
examples.en: I am going to call city hall and ask how to apply.

explain: '질문하다'보다 딱딱해서 국회, 회의, 발표, 공식 문의처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. 친구나 가족에게는 '물어보다'를 써요. '질의응답'은 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '질문하다' and is used in formal settings like the National Assembly, meetings, presentations and official inquiries. With friends or family, use '물어보다'. '질의응답' (Q&A) is a common partner word.

examples.en: I listen to the news on the radio every morning.
A session to hear citizens' opinions will be held.
At the meeting, we heard out the employees' complaints.

examples.ko: 음악을 청취하며 공부하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If I study while listening to music, I cannot concentrate.
People who listened to the broadcast sent in their stories.
Tomorrow we will hear the expert's explanation.

explain: '듣다'보다 격식 있는 말이라서 방송, 회의, 공청회에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '듣다'를 쓰면 돼요. 기관이나 윗사람이 '의견을 청취하다'처럼 사람들의 말을 들을 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '듣다' and is used for broadcasts, meetings, and public hearings. In daily conversation just use '듣다'. Organizations and officials often use it, as in '의견을 청취하다'.

dis.h: formal verb, for broadcasts or hearings

p.n: Same meaning; 듣다 is plain and everyday.
